newsitem.title: USA: Republicans urge passage of flex time bill.
newsitem.headline: Republicans urge passage of flex time bill.

text.p: Republicans want to help American families by passing legislation that would give parents more time off from work to be with their children, Sen. Bill Frist said Saturday.

"The Republican Congress will help hard-pressed families in a very simple way -- we can give them more time together as a family," Frist, of Tennessee, said in the Republican response to President Clinton's weekly radio address.
The bill would allow workers and employers to agree on flexible work schedules and let employees take take off in place of extra pay for overtime.
The bill, called the Family-Friendly Workplace Act, or the flex-time bill, has passed the House and is being considered by the Senate.
But labour unions oppose the measure, saying it would be used to pressure workers to take compensatory time off rather than overtime pay and weaken the standard 40-hour work week.
Clinton said Friday he will veto the bill unless it is changed to provide more protection against abuses by employers.
Frist said pressures on families because fathers and mothers were working longer were contributing to increasing crime and drug use by children.
"The American family is our children's grounding. But more and more, our kids are finding that ground slipping out from underneath them," Frist said.

"What the American family needs most is the gift of time," he said. "What parent wouldn't want time off to attend a parent-teacher meeting or attend their child's award ceremony at school? Or take them to the local library? But what parent can afford to?

"Mending the broken American family is the first step toward winning the battle for our children's future. By giving time back to our families, the flex-time bill is strong ammunition in this fight. So as we celebrate Mother's Day, let's remember that the most precious gift we can give our parents is a bright future for their children," Frist said.
